messages:
rajesh: Heads-up — got repeated DCGM/ECC/Xid noise on gpu-node-42 this morning. Alert fired and the auto-drain playbook started. ~7 Xid events across gpu0/gpu2 in ~5m. Current rule: threshold 3 events / 60s. Do we want to tune suppression or the drain policy? :thinking:

marta: Can you paste the prometheus query and which pool this is in? If it's preemptible we might be overreacting to transient card glitches.

rajesh: Query I used: `sum by(gpu_id) (increase(nvidia_dcgm_gpu_memory_ecc_errors_total[10m]))` — shows gpu0=5, gpu2=3. Pool=cloud-gpu-preemptible. Node has 3 pods evicted so far.

samir: Evictions here matter — those jobs were latency-sensitive, so draining equaled SLA risk. I'd rather we try suppression-first, drain-second. Suggestion: require either (A) >=3 distinct Xid types within 10m OR (B) single Xid with ecc_count>8 in 5m. That avoids 1-off kernel spew causing a full node swap.

marta: Strong +1. Also propose hysteresis: when a node previously had a swap in last 24h, keep stricter thresholds (shorter suppression window). If it's a first-time flare, allow longer suppression. We can implement with a recording rule referencing `node_swap_count` metric.

rajesh: Rough prometheus rule draft for experimentation (canary pool only):

```
- alert: GPU_ECC_XID_Problem_Candidate
  expr: |
    (
      sum by(node) (increase(nvidia_dcgm_gpu_memory_ecc_errors_total[10m])) >= 3
    ) or (
      sum by(node) (increase(nvidia_dcgm_gpu_memory_ecc_errors_total[5m])) >= 8
    )
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: warning
  annotations:
    summary: "Candidate GPU ECC/Xid problem on {{ $labels.node }}"
```

Make it fire as `warning` first and only escalate to `critical` if it stays >20m or node_swap_count > 1.

ops-bot: ALERT RECEIVED: gpu-node-42 — 7 Xid events. Automated drain not executed because suppression window config changed.

oncall-rotation: If we roll this, can we canary to the `gpu-small-canary` pool for 24h? Need to monitor QPS and eviction count. Also, please update the oncall runbook to show the new windows and how to force a manual drain if needed.

samir: Agree on canary. I'll push the rule to staging and wire up a Grafana panel showing `increase(...[10m])` per gpu and `node_swap_count`. We'll collect 24h. If no missed errors, roll to prod.

marta: One more: add an annotation with `recovery_playbook: >` linking to the swap versus cordon guidance. Prefer cordon + 15m graceful eviction for latency-sensitive jobs rather than immediate drain. That reduces capacity churn and cost.

rajesh: Noted. Also raising a cost/availability note: frequent false-positive drains are eating into our reserved capacity headroom and forcing extra burst instances in eu-west-1 last week. If suppression reduces churn, we save ~2-3% on monthly infra spend for that region.

oncall-rotation: Action items pinned: 1) samir to deploy canary rule to `gpu-small-canary` by EOD, 2) marta to update runbook and add annotation link, 3) rajesh to run retrospective on last 3 drains and post findings. Revisit in 24h. :white_check_mark:

rajesh: I'll post the drain timeline + pod eviction list to the ticket. Thanks y'all.

marta: If we see sustained increase after canary, we'll tighten windows and consider pro-active card replacement. For now try suppression + staged escalation. :thumbsup:

samir: Deploying now to canary. Will ping when metrics stable or if we see missed real failures.

ops-bot: NOTE: Prometheus rule deployment scheduled to `canary` namespace at 2026-03-18T14:22:00Z.
